title: Extension by zero preserves constant-local-model constructibility
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$, and let $j\colon U\hookrightarrow X$ be an open immersion of separated finite-type $k$-schemes, as in [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], put $\Lambda_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ for $T=U,X$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], and let $j_!\colon\Mod_{\Lambda_U}\to\Mod_{\Lambda_X}$ be the extension by zero of module objects [sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek].

Let $M$ be a $\Lambda_U$-module that is constructible in the sense of [sk-def-sfb-constructible]: there is a finite stratification $U=\coprod_aU_a$ [def-constructible-stratification] by constructible locally closed subschemes such that each $M|_{U_a}$ has a finite constant local model [det-def-sfb-constructible-local-model]. Then $j_!M$ is a constructible $\Lambda_X$-module in the same sense. More precisely, the subschemes $U_a$, viewed in $X$, together with the closed complement $Z=X\setminus U$ with its reduced subscheme structure [def-pc-reduced-scheme], form a finite stratification of $X$ by constructible locally closed subschemes; for every $a$ the restriction $(j_!M)|_{U_a}$ is isomorphic, as a $\Lambda_{U_a}$-module, to $M|_{U_a}$, and $(j_!M)|_Z=0$. The cases $U=\varnothing$ (then $M=0$ and $j_!M=0$) and $U=X$ (then $Z=\varnothing$) are included.

proof.text: Finite type over the field makes X locally Noetherian; quasi-compactness over its compact affine base makes X compact, hence Noetherian. Construct the extended family explicitly with Fin.cases: index zero is j.closedComplement, and index a.succ is S.immersion a followed by j. The image of the complement is the complement of the range of j. The original covering and injectivity of j prove coverage and pairwise disjointness; immersions compose. Every image is locally closed and therefore constructible in X. The equivalence finSuccEquiv identifies these indices with Option (Fin S.n), and the Over-X identifications are reflexive isomorphisms.

The unit of abelian extension by zero is invertible by the open-immersion adjunction triple. The module forgetful functor reflects isomorphisms and identifies the linear-extension unit with that abelian unit. Thus linear extension is fully faithful. Restriction along the invertible coefficient map is an equivalence, so their composite j_! is fully faithful. Its adjunction unit gives j^*j_!M isomorphic to M. Apply pullback composition and map this isomorphism along each S.immersion a to obtain the asserted stratum isomorphisms. No comparison with sectionwise ringed modules is used.

For a map g with range disjoint from the open, j-restriction of g_*F has sections over empty fibre products. The sheaf axiom for the empty pro-etale cover makes those sections zero. The two abelian adjunctions then identify maps from g^*j_!F with maps into this zero object, so g^*j_!F is initial and hence zero. Apply g=j.closedComplement. Extension along the invertible coefficient morphism is restriction along its inverse on underlying sheaves. Faithfulness of Mod.forget therefore gives the claimed module vanishing.

proof.text: Transport each original finite constant local model along the stratum isomorphism, using the same cover, point module, finite presentation and pulled-back isomorphism. For a zero module use the singleton identity cover and zero point module; the cokernel of the identity of finiteFree Lambda 0 is zero and gives its finite presentation. The additive inverse image from the point and the stratum pullback preserve zero objects. Supply these local models on the explicit constructible stratification to IsFiniteConstantStratified and then the qcqs branch of IsConstantModelConstructible.

If U is empty, the source scheme of every object of U.ProEt is empty, so its sections are zero by the empty-cover sheaf axiom. Faithfulness of the module forgetful functor gives M=0; additive extension sends it to zero. If j is an isomorphism, it is surjective, so the complement-range equality excludes every point of the closed complement. The construction retains empty strata and also works for S.n=0 and X empty.
